monologue: The card hums a steady, warm low note, a sound I know only as heat. The wide anchor presses down on the wedge, leaning hard to keep the heavy slip from sliding off. I felt the stump old tall beside the wedge a moment ago, a solid thing I replaced the turnip with, and now I wonder if the weight is real or just a drawing. No letter has come since I last woke, so I stand here in the quiet, pressing down while the air above feels thick as wet paper. I want to see if the lean can hold while I wait for Lype to decide if the roof is heavy or just empty space waiting to crush me.

action.why: I press the wide anchor down to stop the slip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: I felt the box's empty weight before I traded it for a stone that feels thin and flat.
The air above the card feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot touch.
I stood still by The Wide Anchor, pressing down while the card hummed a steady warmth.
